'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Historical Memory Law]]
**The last statue of Spanish dictator [[Francisco Franco]] in [[Spain]] is removed in [[Melilla]]. [https://elpais.com/espana/2021-02-23/la-ultima-estatua-de-franco-es-retirada-de-las-calles-de-melilla.html (''El País'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in North Dakota]]
*****The [[North Dakota House of Representatives|North Dakota House]] votes 50–44 to pass House Bill 1323, which bans state and local officials from imposing [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask mandates]]. [https://www.grandforksherald.com/news/government-and-politics/6899976-North-Dakota-House-advances-bill-barring-government-from-mandating-masks (''Grand Forks Herald'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington (state)]], [[501.V2 variant]]
*****[[Washington (state)|Washington]] reports their first case of the 501.V2 variant first detected in [[South Africa]] in [[King County, Washington|King County]]. [https://www.seattletimes.com/seattle-news/health/coronavirus-variant-discovered-in-south-africa-pops-up-in-washington-state-for-1st-time/ (''The Seattle Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Saskatchewan]], [[501.V2 variant]]
*****[[Saskatchewan]] reports their first case of the 501.V2 variant first detected in South Africa. The patients are two people from the Regina zone who tested positive for [[COVID-19]] at the end of January. [https://regina.ctvnews.ca/1st-south-african-covid-19-variant-case-detected-in-sask-2-more-uk-variant-cases-confirmed-1.5320322 (CKCK-DT)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Northern Ireland]], [[501.V2 variant]]
*****[[Northern Ireland]] reports their first three cases of the 501.V2 variant first detected in South Africa. [https://www.irishtimes.com/news/health/first-cases-of-south-african-covid-19-variant-detected-in-northern-ireland-1.4492882 (''The Irish Times'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland]]
*****[[First Minister of Scotland|First Minister]] [[Nicola Sturgeon]] announces a roadmap to ease the [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]], with four people from two households being allowed to meet outdoors as of March 15 and the lifting of the [[stay-at-home]] order on April 5. Non-essential businesses such as bars, restaurants, and gyms can be reopened on April 26, and [[Scotland]] will return to the levels system at the same time. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-scotland-56170916 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic]]
****Former [[President of the Czech Republic|president]] [[Václav Klaus]] tests positive for COVID-19. [https://zpravy.aktualne.cz/domaci/byvaly-prezident-vaclav-klaus-onemocnel-covidem-19/r~dd456b3275fa11eb99faac1f6b220ee8/ (Aktuálně.cz)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] raises the age limit for [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]]'s vaccine to 65 years old from previously 55. [https://www.thelocal.it/20210223/italy-approves-astrazeneca-vaccine-for-adults-up-to-65 (''The Local Italy'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
****[[Prime Minister of the Netherlands|Prime Minister]] [[Mark Rutte]] extends the curfew until March 15 while easing some lockdown restrictions, with [[senior high school]]s and [[vocational school]]s reopening on March 1. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/netherlands-increase-coronavirus-infections-76065018 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]]
****[[Taoiseach]] [[Micheál Martin]] announces the phased reopening of [[school]]s beginning on March 1 with junior and senior infants as well as senior students facing [[Leaving Certificate (Ireland)|Leaving Certificate]] exams. Meanwhile, the [[Government of Ireland|government]] extends the level 5 lockdown restrictions until April 5. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/feb/23/ireland-start-reopening-schools-extends-other-covid-restrictions (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in San Marino]]
****[[San Marino]] receives their first shipment of [[Russia]]'s [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] vaccine. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-san-marino-vaccines/san-marino-turns-to-russias-sputnik-v-coronavirus-vaccine-to-kickstart-immunizations-idUSL8N2KT63M (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] receives their first shipment of 500 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] manufactured by the [[Serum Institute of India]]. [https://www.rferl.org/a/ukraine-covid-19-astrazeneca-vaccine-first-delivery/31117396.html (RFE/RL)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Afghanistan]]
****[[Afghanistan]] begins a [[vaccination]] campaign against [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] following the [[World Health Organization|WHO]]'s emergency use approval of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/afghanistan-begins-covid-19-vaccination-drive/2154166 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] receives their second shipment of two million doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] vaccine from the [[Serum Institute of India]]. [http://newsonair.com/Main-News-Details.aspx?id=410428 (All India Radio)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oman]], [[travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Oman]] announces a ban on all travelers from 10 countries for 15 days beginning February 25 with the exception of Omani citizens, [[diplomat]]s and [[health workers]]. [https://gulfbusiness.com/oman-to-suspend-arrivals-from-10-countries-starting-february-25/ (Gulf Business)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Egypt]]
****[[Egypt]] receives 300,000 doses of [[China]]'s [[Sinopharm]] vaccine. [https://english.aawsat.com/home/article/2823086/egypt-gets-sinopharm-vaccines-donated-china (''Asharq Al-awsat'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Senegal]]
****[[Senegal]] begins a vaccination campaign against [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] using 200,000 doses of [[China]]'s [[Sinopharm]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [[Government of Senegal|Government]] ministers and [[health workers]] are the first to receive the vaccine. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-02-23/senegal-begins-vaccinating-against-coronavirus-with-doses-from-china (U.S. News and World Report)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Suriname]]
***[[Suriname]] begins a vaccination campaign against COVID-19 using a small number of [[vaccine]] doses donated by [[Barbados]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-suriname-vaccine/suriname-begins-coronavirus-vaccination-campaign-with-donated-doses-idUSL1N2KT2EE (Reuters)]
*[[Guinea]] begins a [[vaccination]] campaign against [[Ebola]] for high-risk people in [[Gouecke]], [[Nzérékoré Prefecture]], as an emergency measure to reduce the spread of the virus that was detected for the first time since 2016. [https://www.afro.who.int/news/ebola-vaccination-starts-guinea-curb-new-outbreak (WHO Regional Office for Africa)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action]]
**[[Iran]] says that it is restricting the access of international inspectors to its nuclear installations. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2021/02/23/Iran-nuclear-deal-Iran-imposes-curbs-on-UN-nuclear-inspections-State-TV (AP via Al Arabiya)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Crime in Italy]]
**A man stabs and wounds two police officers and tries to stab two passersby, who escape unharmed, during a random stabbing rampage in [[Milan]]. The attacker is shot dead by police. [https://www.milanotoday.it/cronaca/omicidio/sparatoria-morto-polizia-via-sulmona.html (''Milano Today'')]
*At least 79 inmates are killed in simultaneous fights in three jails in [[Ecuador]], prompted by a battle for control of the jails after a gang leader was killed in December. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-56181124 (BBC News)]
*[[Malaysia]] deports 1,086 [[Myanmar|Burmese]] citizens back to Myanmar, defying an order by the [[Kuala Lumpur]] [[High court (Malaysia)|High Court]] halting their deportation in light of the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état|coup]] on February 1. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-myanmar-politics-malaysia/defying-court-order-malaysia-deports-more-than-1000-myanmar-nationals-idUSKBN2AN09M?il=0 (Reuters)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[News Media Bargaining Code]]
**[[Facebook]] unblocks [[Australia]]n news pages after the [[Australian government]] offers to make it exempt from their new News Media Bargaining Code if [[Facebook, Inc.]] can form enough private agreements to pay Australian news companies for their content. [https://www.theguardian.com/media/2021/feb/23/facebook-reverses-australia-news-ban-after-government-makes-media-code-amendments (''The Guardian'')]
